criteria.rationale: Compared both trailer parsers and verified the shared-order subsequence premise in spec_trailers.go:31-66. Independently ran digest-equivalence, read-count, and failed-stream tests. Corpus byte-identity and timing remain implementer-reported measurements, not independently repeated benchmarks. Duplicate trailers deliberately retain per-spec reads. The local broader-test failure is the pre-existing rendering assertion recorded as F1.

The new hash maps and writers are local to a synchronous collection call. No goroutines or shared mutable state were introduced. changeSetGitStream preserves the timeout, cancellation cleanup, and existing read-view lifecycle.
Digest computation and change-set construction retain their existing formulas and fields; only internal patch acquisition changes.

Reviewed existing slug and revision validation, bounded history and patch reads, and error wrapping. artifact_integrity.go:466-478 excludes failed digests; lines 676-678 preserve the cause as a collection gap. The failed-stream regression passed locally.

The production collector invokes the shared pass at artifact_integrity.go:673 and consumes its digests at line 680. The collector performance test exercises this composition for multiple specs and passed locally.
The extracted stream helper retains bounded stderr and wrapped forensic causes. Collection errors retain spec context, and failed partial hashes are not published.

Examined parser semantics, Git arguments, digest substitution, and returned ChangeSet fields. Public CLI, MCP, and serialized file contracts remain unchanged; duplicate trailer semantics are preserved through fallback.

D1 selects ordered fan-out because repeated patch reads arise from per-spec collection. artifact_integrity.go:437-478 streams each eligible commit into all owning hashes, addressing R1 without retaining patch bytes. Duplicate detection implements R3; the resolver consumes the precomputed digest for R2; failure fan-out and collection gaps implement R4. No individual structural-fact deltas were supplied in the brief.

Compared the spec, implementation comments, and validation-matrix addition. The SinglePass selector matches the new test. Documentation accurately describes duplicate-trailer fallback, unchanged final audit, and absence of persistent caching.

Reviewed cause preservation and spec-specific collection gaps. Existing actionable revision and history errors remain available; the optimization introduces no configuration, migration, or recovery procedure.

R1/R2 have shared-commit count and digest-equivalence coverage; R3 has duplicate-trailer exclusion and unchanged per-spec fallback; R4 has failed-stream regression coverage and explicit fan-out inspection at artifact_integrity.go:466-478,676-678. Focused tests passed locally. The corpus comparison is recorded in the spec execution log.

Compared the requested range and declared artifacts against R1-R4. Implementation changes remain confined to ordered trailer parsing, shared digest collection, resolver integration, and regression/performance checks. No unrelated production refactor or public contract change was introduced.

Reviewed changed Git invocations and stream plumbing. Raw-history protections, argument-based process execution, byte bounds, timeout, read-view binding, and final audit remain intact. No new authority boundary, dependency, persistent cache, or sensitive logging was introduced.

Compared D1's alternatives. Ordered MultiWriter fan-out is sufficient because every spec's commit sequence derives from the same log; retaining patch bytes or persisting digests would add unnecessary storage and invalidation concerns. The duplicate-trailer fallback avoids a more complex replay mechanism. Revisit this choice if attribution sequences cease to be subsequences of one shared log.

Under a UTF-8 locale, cmdCheck correctly emits '⚠ warning', but TestCheckRefusesAnIndexSetThatItsDescriptorDoesNotDescribe fails at line 47. Reproduced both in the broader test run and in isolation; git show of the base commit confirms the helper is unchanged. This does not invalidate the single-pass implementation or the sealed validation results.
